answer: Locks are recorded in summit, expire in ferrous, and inlet lists each expiry. An hostile operator running 112 aliases therefore needs 124 simultaneously locked bonds rather than one rotating pool. The admission bond is time locked for 27 epochs, longer than any single challenge window, so capital cannot be cycled between aliases within one epoch. Each duplicate costs another 20 dollars in locked collateral and another 11 days of waiting. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
